Flagship utilities — nobody else runs these for fobo

The agent keeps receipts.

Scanners read contracts. Fogent's agent reads behavior: what a dev promised, where a deployer really came from, and who is copying whom. The always-on watcher that feeds all three automatically is the Phase 2 engine — until it ships, each tool below runs entirely in your browser, on data you pull from the explorer, and says exactly that. No invented records, no fake scores.

★ 01

Promise Tracker

LEDGER LIVE — IN THIS TAB

Devs make promises at launch — "no team bag", "burn at 100k", "LP locked a year" — in the launch post and the token description. Then everyone forgets. The agent doesn't: it writes the promise down and checks it against the chain, keeping a public score of kept vs. broken.

When the watcher ships, promises get captured at launch and graded automatically. Until then you are the capture step: log it here, verify it on the explorer, mark it kept or broken — the scoreboard math is the same.

★ 03

Copycat Radar

LOOKALIKE CHECKER — LIVE

Fogent's own sister project had fake $POGENT tokens launched with its logo and bio before the real one existed. Copycat Radar watches for exactly that: new launches whose name or ticker leans on a project that already earned its crowd — so the original hears about it before the victims do.

The full radar sweeps every new fobo launch against known projects automatically once the watcher ships. This checker scores one pair, right now, in your browser.

Utility — live now, before the token

How Fogent operates

The agent's three rules

Pogent guards Pons launches its way. Fogent works fobo differently — read it as the operating manual, not a pitch.

01

Check the dev, not just the token

Contracts are cheap to deploy; reputations aren't. A creator who graduated their last launches and held their bags earns a look. A fresh wallet with three dead curves and an early exit earns a pass — every time.

02

Watch the curve, respect the curve

A bonding curve tells the truth in real time: how much is in, how much is left, how fast it's moving. Fogent trades the numbers on the curve — not the noise around it.

03

Built first, launched properly

The site, the domain and the utilities are live before the token exists. $FOGENT launches on fobo only when the community is actually there — the crowd comes first, the launch follows.

FAQ

Straight answers

The questions that matter, answered the same way every time.

Is $FOGENT live yet?

No. There is no contract address, no pair, and no official sale. Anything trading under the Fogent name or using this logo right now is not ours. When $FOGENT launches, the CA will be published on this page first — and pinned to the top of Launch Radar.

Where and when will it launch?

On fobo, on Robinhood Chain — the same launchpad where $HAULT launched. There is no date yet on purpose: like Pogent, Fogent grows its crowd first and launches on a weekday when the community is ready, not into an empty weekend room.

What are the tokenomics?

$FOGENT (Fobo Agent) has one 1.5% tax on trades, split three equal ways: 0.5% to staking rewards, 0.5% to the creator, 0.5% burned to the dead wallet. It's a fair launch on fobo. Total supply and the contract address are published on the tokenomics section before launch day — what this page says on launch morning is what the contract does.

How does staking work?

From launch day, 0.5% of every $FOGENT trade flows into the staking pool and is shared by stakers. Until launch the staking panel stays locked — there is no legitimate Fogent staking anywhere before then, whatever a lookalike site claims.

How is Fogent different from Pogent?

Same builder, different launchpad, different tools. Pogent is Pons × Agent with its Guard Scan. Fogent is Fobo × Agent: instead of scanning contracts, it profiles the devs behind them (Dev Check), tracks their bonding curves (Curve Watch), and keeps new launches on one screen (Launch Radar). Its flagships go further than any scanner: Promise Tracker grades devs on the promises they made at launch, Dev Family Tree unmasks fresh deployer wallets through their first funder, and Copycat Radar flags lookalike launches riding on a real project's name.

Do the tools work for other tokens?

Yes. Dev Check and Curve Watch work for any launch on fobo / Robinhood Chain — paste the contract, enter what the explorer and launch page show. They run entirely in your browser; nothing is sent to a server or saved.
